/** Specifies the Major type of ::cbor_item_t */
typedef enum cbor_type {
  CBOR_TYPE_UINT /** 0 - positive integers */
  ,
  CBOR_TYPE_NEGINT /** 1 - negative integers*/
  ,
  CBOR_TYPE_BYTESTRING /** 2 - byte strings */
  ,
  CBOR_TYPE_STRING /** 3 - strings */
  ,
  CBOR_TYPE_ARRAY /** 4 - arrays */
  ,
  CBOR_TYPE_MAP /** 5 - maps */
  ,
  CBOR_TYPE_TAG /** 6 - tags  */
  ,
  CBOR_TYPE_FLOAT_CTRL /** 7 - decimals and special values (true, false, nil,
                          ...) */
} cbor_type;
objects.description: Enum of CBOR major types as used by cbor_item_t for discriminating the union metadata and data interpretation.

Enum indicating the storage width for floating point and control CBOR items.
Enum marking definite vs. indefinite length encoding for dynamic-size CBOR types.
Enum of CBOR simple control values as they appear in the encoded stream.
Per-item metadata for integer CBOR items, currently tracking width.
Metadata for CBOR byte strings, including length and definite/indefinite flag.
Metadata for CBOR text strings, tracking byte length, Unicode code point count (for indefinite strings sum), and definite/indefinite flag.
Metadata for CBOR arrays, including capacity/allocation, current end index, and definite/indefinite flag.
Metadata for CBOR maps, including capacity/allocation, current end index, and definite/indefinite flag.
Metadata for CBOR tags, storing the tag numeric value and a pointer to the tagged item when present.
Metadata for floating point and control items, indicating float width and raw control value when applicable.
Helper union for bit-level casting between float and uint32_t representations.
Helper union for bit-level casting between double and uint64_t representations.

functions.name: cbor_load
functions.signature: _CBOR_NODISCARD CBOR_EXPORT cbor_item_t* cbor_load(cbor_data source, size_t source_size, struct cbor_load_result* result);
functions.description: Decode a single CBOR data item from a memory buffer. On success returns a newly created cbor_item_t with reference count initialized to one. On failure returns NULL and writes error details (location/description) to result. Typical usage: pass a pointer to the CBOR byte stream and its size, and inspect result on failure. Caller owns the returned item and must manage its lifetime.
requirements: source must point to a readable buffer containing at least source_size bytes.
source_size must accurately reflect the number of bytes available at source for decoding.
result must point to writable storage for a struct cbor_load_result to receive status information (on success set to CBOR_ERR_NONE; on failure contains error details).
The returned item (on success) has reference count 1; the caller is responsible for releasing it per the library's reference-counting API.
If NULL is returned, the caller must not attempt to use the item pointer.

functions.name: cbor_copy
functions.description: Create a deep copy of the given CBOR item. All referenced sub-items (arrays, maps, string chunks, tagged items) are recursively duplicated so the new structure shares no storage with the original. The new item's reference count is initialized to one. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: item must be a valid pointer to an existing cbor_item_t.
The returned item (on success) has reference count 1; the caller must release it using the library's reference-counting/freeing functions.
On NULL return (allocation failure), the caller must treat the operation as failed and not use the returned pointer.

functions.name: cbor_copy_definite
functions.description: Deep-copy a CBOR item while converting all indefinite-length constructs to their definite-length equivalents. Semantics otherwise mirror cbor_copy. Returns a new item with reference count set to one, or NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: item must be a valid pointer to an existing cbor_item_t.
The returned item (on success) has reference count 1; the caller must release it using the library's reference-counting/freeing functions.
On NULL return (allocation failure), the caller must treat the operation as failed and not use the returned pointer.

functions.name: cbor_describe
functions.signature: CBOR_EXPORT void cbor_describe(cbor_item_t* item, FILE* out);
functions.description: Pretty-print a human-readable description of a CBOR item to the given FILE stream. Intended for debugging and inspection. Note: this API is only available when compiled with CBOR_PRETTY_PRINTER enabled.
requirements: This function is available only when the library is built with CBOR_PRETTY_PRINTER enabled; callers must ensure the symbol is present at compile/link time.
item must be a valid pointer to a cbor_item_t to be described.
out must be a valid FILE* opened for writing (e.g., stdout, stderr, or a writable file).

functions.name: cbor_array_size
functions.description: Returns the number of elements currently stored in a CBOR array item. Use to query logical size before indexed access or iteration.
requirements: item must be a valid, initialized CBOR array (cbor_item_t) created by libcbor.
Returns the number of members; no side effects.
If item is not an array, behavior is undefined by this header (caller must ensure correct type).

functions.name: cbor_array_allocated
functions.description: Returns the number of element slots currently allocated for the array’s storage (capacity), which may be >= size.
requirements: item must be a valid, initialized CBOR array (cbor_item_t) created by libcbor.
Result is the allocated capacity; do not assume it equals cbor_array_size().

functions.name: cbor_array_get
functions.signature: cbor_item_t* cbor_array_get(const cbor_item_t* item, size_t index);
functions.description: Returns a reference to the array element at the given zero-based index, or NULL if the index is out of bounds. The function increments the referenced item’s refcount; the caller must release it with cbor_decref when done.
requirements: item must be a valid CBOR array.
index must be within [0, cbor_array_size(item)) to succeed; otherwise NULL is returned.
On success, the returned cbor_item_t* has its reference count increased; the caller must call cbor_decref on the pointer when finished.
Caller must check for NULL before dereferencing the returned pointer.

functions.name: cbor_array_set
functions.signature: bool cbor_array_set(cbor_item_t* item, size_t index, cbor_item_t* value);
functions.description: Assigns value to the element at the given zero-based index. Fails and leaves the array unmodified if the index is out of bounds. Arrays with holes are not allowed. On success, increments value’s refcount by one.
requirements: item must be a valid, mutable CBOR array.
value must be a valid cbor_item_t*; its reference count will be increased by one on success.
index must refer to a valid position without creating holes; out-of-bounds indices cause the function to return false and leave the array unchanged.
Returns true on success; returns false on allocation failure or invalid index (out of bounds).
Caller does not need to adjust the previous element’s refcount (no replacement semantics implied beyond setting); existing element’s handling beyond bounds check is as defined by the library.
Caller should handle a false return without assuming partial modification.

functions.name: cbor_array_replace
functions.signature: bool cbor_array_replace(cbor_item_t* item, size_t index, cbor_item_t* value);
functions.description: Replaces the element at index with value. Increments value’s refcount by one, and releases the reference to the element being replaced using cbor_decref. Returns true on success, false on allocation failure.
requirements: item must be a valid, mutable CBOR array.
index must be a valid position within the array; replacing out-of-bounds is not defined to succeed.
value must be a valid cbor_item_t*; its reference count is increased by one on success.
The previously stored element (if any) will be decref’d by the function; callers must not decref it again to avoid double-free.
Caller must handle false return (allocation failure) without assuming modification occurred.

functions.name: cbor_array_is_definite
functions.description: Returns true if the CBOR array uses definite-length encoding; false otherwise.
requirements: item must be a valid CBOR array.

functions.name: cbor_array_is_indefinite
functions.description: Returns true if the CBOR array uses indefinite-length encoding; false otherwise.
requirements: item must be a valid CBOR array.

functions.name: cbor_array_handle
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal array of element pointers. Callers may reorder or modify the items as long as reference consistency is maintained. The array length is cbor_array_size(item).
requirements: item must be a valid CBOR array.

The returned pointer refers to internal storage; modifying it requires maintaining reference-count and pointer consistency (do not leak or double-free; adjust refcounts appropriately if you change elements).
The caller must not use indices beyond cbor_array_size(item).
Do not free the returned pointer; it is owned by the array and may become invalid if the array is reallocated or destroyed.

functions.name: cbor_new_definite_array
functions.description: Creates a new definite-length CBOR array with storage preallocated for size elements. The returned item’s reference count is initialized to one. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: size is the number of slots to preallocate (capacity).
On success, the caller owns a reference with refcount = 1 and must eventually call cbor_decref on the array when done.
Caller must check for NULL to handle allocation failure before using the result.

functions.name: cbor_new_indefinite_array
functions.description: Creates a new indefinite-length CBOR array. The returned item’s reference count is initialized to one. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: On success, the caller owns a reference with refcount = 1 and must eventually call cbor_decref on the array when done.
Caller must check for NULL to handle allocation failure before using the result.

functions.name: cbor_array_push
functions.description: Appends pushee to the end of the array. For indefinite arrays, storage may be reallocated. For definite arrays, only the preallocated capacity is usable. Increases pushee’s refcount by one on success. Returns true on success, false on failure.
requirements: array must be a valid, mutable CBOR array.
pushee must be a valid cbor_item_t*; on success its reference count is incremented by one.
For definite arrays, there must be remaining preallocated capacity; otherwise the operation fails (returns false).
For indefinite arrays, callers should not rely on the array_handle pointer remaining valid across pushes, as storage may be reallocated.
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect failure; no partial modification is implied on failure.

functions.name: cbor_bytestring_length
functions.description: Returns the length (in bytes) of the binary payload of a definite CBOR byte string. For newly created items with no data attached the length is 0. Use on definite byte strings only.
requirements: item must be a CBOR byte string item that is definite (not indefinite).
If called on a non-bytestring or an indefinite item, behavior is unspecified by this header.
Caller should treat the return value as the current size; 0 may indicate no data assigned yet.

functions.name: cbor_bytestring_is_definite
functions.description: Checks whether a CBOR byte string item is definite-length.
requirements: item should be a CBOR byte string item.
Return value must be checked to determine definiteness.

functions.name: cbor_bytestring_is_indefinite
functions.description: Checks whether a CBOR byte string item is indefinite-length.
requirements: item should be a CBOR byte string item.
Return value must be checked to determine indefiniteness.

functions.name: cbor_bytestring_handle
functions.description: Returns a mutable pointer to the underlying data buffer of a definite CBOR byte string. Modifying the referenced memory is allowed; the caller assumes responsibility for the effect on any composed items referencing this item. Returns NULL if no data have been assigned.
requirements: item must be a definite CBOR byte string.
The returned pointer may be NULL if no data are assigned; caller must check for NULL before dereferencing.
If the caller modifies the memory, they are responsible for any side effects on containers or other structures referencing this item.

functions.name: cbor_bytestring_set_handle
functions.signature: CBOR_EXPORT void cbor_bytestring_set_handle(cbor_item_t* item, cbor_mutable_data CBOR_RESTRICT_POINTER data, size_t length);
functions.description: Sets the data buffer (handle) and length of a definite CBOR byte string. Ownership of the provided memory block is transferred to libcbor, which will free it using the allocator configured via cbor_set_allocs.
requirements: item must be a definite CBOR byte string.
Caller must provide a memory block data of at least length bytes.
Ownership of data is transferred to libcbor; the caller must not free or reuse it after the call.
Length must describe the size in bytes of the provided block.
libcbor will deallocate the block using the free implementation configured via cbor_set_allocs.
Behavior for NULL data is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: cbor_bytestring_chunks_handle
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal array of chunk items for an indefinite CBOR byte string. The caller may manipulate the memory block (e.g., sort pointers), but must retain the validity of elements and the number of chunks.
requirements: item must be an indefinite CBOR byte string.
Caller may reorder or otherwise manipulate the array storage, but must not change the number of chunks nor invalidate stored chunk pointers.
The number of accessible elements is cbor_bytestring_chunk_count(item).

functions.name: cbor_bytestring_chunk_count
functions.description: Returns the number of chunks in an indefinite CBOR byte string. Freshly created items have a count of 0.
requirements: item should be an indefinite CBOR byte string.
Caller should use this value to bound iteration over the array returned by cbor_bytestring_chunks_handle.

functions.name: cbor_bytestring_add_chunk
functions.signature: CBOR_EXPORT bool cbor_bytestring_add_chunk(cbor_item_t* item, cbor_item_t* chunk);
functions.description: Appends a definite byte-string chunk to an indefinite CBOR byte string. On success, increases the chunk’s reference count by one. May reallocate the internal chunk storage. Returns false if reallocation fails; in that case, the item is unchanged and the chunk’s refcount is not increased.
requirements: item must be an indefinite CBOR byte string.
chunk must be a definite CBOR byte string.
Caller must check the boolean return value for allocation failure.
On success, ownership is shared: the chunk’s refcount is incremented by one.
On failure, neither item nor chunk refcounts are modified (item remains intact).

functions.name: cbor_new_definite_bytestring
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new definite CBOR byte string item. The data handle is initialized to NULL and length to 0. The item’s reference count is initialized to one. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: Caller must check for NULL to detect allocation failure.
Returned item starts with refcount 1; caller is responsible for subsequent reference management per libcbor’s conventions.
Initial data handle is NULL and length is 0 until set with cbor_bytestring_set_handle or similar.

functions.name: cbor_new_indefinite_bytestring
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new indefinite CBOR byte string item. The chunks array is initialized to NULL and the chunk count to 0. The item’s reference count is initialized to one. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: Caller must check for NULL to detect allocation failure.
Returned item starts with refcount 1; caller is responsible for subsequent reference management per libcbor’s conventions.
Initial chunks handle is NULL and chunk count is 0; chunks can be added via cbor_bytestring_add_chunk.

functions.name: cbor_build_bytestring
functions.signature: CBOR_EXPORT cbor_item_t* cbor_build_bytestring(cbor_data handle, size_t length);
functions.description: Constructs a new definite CBOR byte string by copying the provided data buffer into newly allocated memory. The item’s reference count is initialized to one. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: handle must point to at least length bytes of readable data at the time of the call; the function copies the data.
Caller must check for NULL to detect allocation failure.
Resulting item is definite and owns its internal copy; the caller retains ownership of the original handle buffer.

item should not be NULL

item should not be NULL

functions.signature: _CBOR_NODISCARD CBOR_EXPORT struct cbor_decoder_result cbor_stream_decode(cbor_data source, size_t source_size, const struct cbor_callbacks* callbacks, void* context)
functions.description: Stateless CBOR decoder that attempts to parse one CBOR item from the given input buffer and invokes the appropriate callback(s) from the provided callback bundle on success. It decodes exactly one item per call and performs no memory allocations. Typical usage is to repeatedly call this function on a byte buffer (e.g., a stream) while inspecting the returned cbor_decoder_result to determine parse status and how much of the input was consumed; pass an application-defined context pointer that will be forwarded to callbacks.
requirements: source points to the start of the input buffer; it should reference at least source_size bytes.
source_size specifies the exact number of bytes available in source; provide 0 if no data is available.
callbacks must be a valid pointer to a properly initialized struct cbor_callbacks; its function pointers should be prepared to be called according to the kinds of CBOR items present in source.
context may be NULL or any user-defined pointer; it is passed through to callbacks.
The caller should examine the returned struct cbor_decoder_result to determine whether decoding succeeded, failed, or requires more data, and how many bytes were consumed.
Only one CBOR item is decoded per call; if more data follows, the caller must invoke the function again with the remaining bytes.
No dynamic memory allocations occur within this function; do not rely on side effects that would require allocations in the decoder.

functions.description: Decreases the reference count by one but never deallocates the item even if it would reach zero; returns the same item. Intended to transfer ownership to APIs that will incref their arguments (a move-like helper).
requirements: item must be a valid cbor_item_t pointer.
Caller must ensure that the item is later incref’d by the receiving API; otherwise, memory will be leaked (explicit warning).
Use only with functions that incref their arguments; do not use arbitrarily.

data_types.description: A byte buffer containing CBOR-encoded data (Concise Binary Object Representation, RFC 8949). The data may represent any single CBOR item (integers, strings, arrays, maps, tags, floats, simple values). Consumers interpret it as a CBOR byte stream; it need not be well-formed for fuzzing.

An opaque byte buffer with no required encoding or character set. It may contain any values including NUL bytes and non-UTF-8 sequences. Used where APIs accept raw bytes (e.g., byte strings or generic buffers).

A null-terminated text string expected to be valid UTF-8 and to contain no embedded NUL bytes. Suitable for C APIs that take const char* C-strings; typically composed of printable characters but any valid UTF-8 is acceptable as long as it is NUL-terminated and has no interior NULs.

import random
import struct
import itertools

# Generator for CBOR-related fuzzers expecting arbitrary binary data buffers.
# Target stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR to obtain raw bytes used to build or set
# CBOR byte and text strings. We return valid, interesting binary payloads that
# exercise various lengths and byte distributions while remaining valid inputs
# (no malformed container framing is needed because stubs copy raw bytes directly).

MAX_OUT = 4096

def _rng(seed: int) -> random.Random:
    return random.Random(seed)

# Useful byte patterns
_ASCII_TEXTS = [
    b"", b"a", b"hello", b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog",
    b"0" * 64, b"1" * 127, b"2" * 255,
]
_UTF8_TEXTS = [
    "", "\u0000", "\u00A9", "\u2603", "\u20AC", "Hola, mundo",
    "Привет мир", "こんにちは世界", "안녕하세요 세계", "你好，世界",
]
_BIN_PATTERNS = [
    bytes(range(0, 256)),                 # ascending 0..255
    bytes(reversed(range(0, 256))),       # descending 255..0
    b"\x00" * 512,                        # all zeros
    b"\xFF" * 512,                        # all 0xFF
    b"\xAA\x55" * 256,                   # checkerboard
    b"\x00\xFF\x7F\x80" * 128,         # edge bytes repeated
]

# Create a bytes object of a target length using a chosen strategy
def _make_payload(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    mode = r.randrange(8)
    if mode == 0:
        # ASCII text truncated/padded
        base = r.choice(_ASCII_TEXTS)
        return (base * (target_len // (len(base) or 1) + 1))[:target_len]
    elif mode == 1:
        # UTF-8 strings concatenated (valid UTF-8)
        parts = []
        while sum(len(p) for p in parts) < target_len:
            s = r.choice(_UTF8_TEXTS)
            parts.append(s.encode('utf-8'))
        return b"".join(parts)[:target_len]
    elif mode == 2:
        # Binary pattern slice
        base = r.choice(_BIN_PATTERNS)
        if len(base) >= target_len:
            start = r.randrange(0, len(base) - target_len + 1)
            return base[start:start+target_len]
        return (base * (target_len // len(base) + 1))[:target_len]
    elif mode == 3:
        # Random bytes with full 0..255 distribution
        return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(target_len))
    elif mode == 4:
        # Structured: length-prefix followed by payload (opaque to stubs but valid bytes)
        core_len = max(0, target_len - 2)
        core = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(core_len))
        prefix = struct.pack('>H', core_len & 0xFFFF)
        return (prefix + core)[:target_len]
    elif mode == 5:
        # Repeating run of a small alphabet
        alphabet = bytes(sorted(r.sample(range(256), k=r.randrange(2, 8))))
        return bytes(alphabet[i % len(alphabet)] for i in range(target_len))
    elif mode == 6:
        # Mixed valid UTF-8 and invalid sequences (still arbitrary bytes)
        chunks = []
        while sum(len(c) for c in chunks) < target_len:
            if r.random() < 0.5:
                # valid utf-8 chunk
                s = r.choice(_UTF8_TEXTS).encode('utf-8')
                chunks.append(s)
            else:
                # invalid byte sequences (e.g., lone continuation bytes)
                bad_len = r.randrange(1, 5)
                bad = bytes(r.randrange(0x80, 0xC0) for _ in range(bad_len))
                chunks.append(bad)
        return b"".join(chunks)[:target_len]
    else:
        # Mode 7: High-entropy head and tail with patterned middle
        if target_len <= 8:
            return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(target_len))
        head = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(4))
        tail = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(4))
        mid_len = target_len - 8
        mid = (b"\x00\xFF" * ((mid_len + 1)//2))[:mid_len]
        return head + mid + tail

# Choose an interesting length respecting stub limits
# - bytestring_set_handle caps to 1..1024
# - build_bytestring caps to 1..1024 and forces non-zero
# - string_set_handle uses 0..1024 (allows zero)
# - callbacks may cap to 0..2048, but they also just read the FUZZ_PARAM_STR
#   into a temporary and possibly resize; any length up to 2048 is fine.
# We therefore bias lengths around 0, 1, small, boundary (255/256/1024), and random up to 2048.

def _choose_length(r: random.Random) -> int:
    choice = r.randrange(10)
    if choice == 0:
        return 0
    if choice == 1:
        return 1
    if choice == 2:
        return 16
    if choice == 3:
        return 255
    if choice == 4:
        return 256
    if choice == 5:
        return 512
    if choice == 6:
        return 1024
    if choice == 7:
        return 2048
    # random in [0, 2048]
    return r.randrange(0, 2049)

# Compose multiple segments to increase variety while staying under MAX_OUT

def _compose_buffer(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    segments = []
    total = 0
    # 1 to 3 segments
    for _ in range(1 + r.randrange(3)):
        remaining = min(2048, MAX_OUT - total)
        if remaining <= 0:
            break
        target_len = min(_choose_length(r), remaining)
        seg = _make_payload(r, target_len)
        segments.append(seg)
        total += len(seg)
    data = b"".join(segments)
    # Ensure length constraints for stubs that expect non-empty sometimes: FUZZ_PARAM_STR is used
    # and stubs often handle zero-length by substituting or allow zero. Zero is acceptable, but
    # to maximize coverage we produce non-empty most of the time.
    if not data:
        data = b"x"
    # Clamp hard limit
    return data[:MAX_OUT]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = _rng(seed)
    return _compose_buffer(r)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: UTF-8 string without NULs, null-terminated expected by cbor_build_string.
# The fuzzer stub pulls FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and then maps bytes to printable ASCII [32,126],
# skipping embedded NULs, and ensures non-empty by inserting 'A' if empty.
# To maximize interesting behavior while remaining valid, we generate diverse printable UTF-8
# strings (ASCII subset), sometimes including multi-byte UTF-8 (still without NULs), and keep size <= 1024.
# The stub will further map bytes, but providing already-valid, varied inputs helps exercise paths
# like length handling and different character distributions.

PRINTABLE_ASCII = ''.join(chr(i) for i in range(32, 127))  # 95 chars

# Some useful UTF-8 multi-byte code point ranges (exclude NUL):
# - Latin-1 supplement (U+00A1..U+00FF) -> 2-byte
# - Greek/Cyrillic snippets (U+0370..U+03FF, U+0400..U+04FF)
# - Emoji (U+1F300..U+1F6FF) -> 4-byte
MULTI_RANGES = [
    (0x00A1, 0x00FF),
    (0x0100, 0x017F),  # Latin Extended-A
    (0x0370, 0x03FF),  # Greek
    (0x0400, 0x04FF),  # Cyrillic
    (0x20AC, 0x20CF),  # Currency symbols vicinity
    (0x1F300, 0x1F64F),  # Misc symbols and emoticons subset
]

def _rand_printable_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_utf8_codepoint(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose either printable ASCII or a multi-byte code point
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(PRINTABLE_ASCII)
    lo, hi = rng.choice(MULTI_RANGES)
    cp = rng.randint(lo, hi)
    try:
        ch = chr(cp)
        # Ensure it encodes in UTF-8 without errors
        ch.encode('utf-8')
        return ch
    except Exception:
        # Fallback to ASCII if encoding fails for some reason
        return rng.choice(PRINTABLE_ASCII)

def _pattern_ascii_blocks(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create blocks to exercise different lengths and repeats
    parts: List[str] = []
    # Edge short strings
    parts.append('A')
    parts.append('AB')
    parts.append('Hello, CBOR!')
    # Repeated characters
    ch = rng.choice(PRINTABLE_ASCII)
    parts.append(ch * rng.randint(3, 32))
    # Mixed digits/letters/symbols
    sym = '!@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{};:,<.>/?\\|'  # all printable
    pool = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + sym
    parts.append(''.join(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(rng.randint(10, 40))))
    return ''.join(parts)

def _pattern_utf8_mixed(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    # Build a mixed string approaching target_len characters (not bytes)
    s = []
    while len(s) < target_len:
        s.append(_rand_utf8_codepoint(rng))
    return ''.join(s)

def _make_cases(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    cases: List[str] = []

    # 1) Small ASCII strings
    cases.append('A')
    cases.append('CBOR')
    cases.append('The quick brown fox')

    # 2) Patterned ASCII blocks
    cases.append(_pattern_ascii_blocks(rng))

    # 3) Long ASCII near stub cap (<=1024)
    long_len = rng.randint(900, 1024)
    cases.append(_rand_printable_ascii(rng, long_len))

    # 4) Mixed UTF-8 multi-byte content of moderate size
    cases.append(_pattern_utf8_mixed(rng, rng.randint(50, 150)))

    # 5) Repeated sequences to test mapping
    base = 'XYZ123!'
    cases.append(base * rng.randint(30, 120))

    # 6) JSON-like content (still ASCII)
    jsonish = '{"type":"cbor","valid":true,"n":12345,"s":"hello"}'
    cases.append(jsonish)

    # 7) Path-like and URL-like content
    cases.append('/usr/local/bin/cbor_tool')
    cases.append('https://example.com/cbor?x=1&y=2#frag')

    # 8) Balanced brackets and diverse symbols
    cases.append('[({<CBOR>})]=+-*/^~`')

    # 9) Emoji-heavy
    emoji_row = ''.join(chr(cp) for cp in range(0x1F600, 0x1F64F))  # emoticons block subset
    # Trim to a reasonable size
    emoji_pick = ''.join(rng.choice(emoji_row) for _ in range(rng.randint(16, 64)))
    cases.append(emoji_pick)

    # 10) Alternating ASCII and multi-byte
    alt = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(40, 120)):
        alt.append(rng.choice(PRINTABLE_ASCII))
        alt.append(_rand_utf8_codepoint(rng))
    cases.append(''.join(alt))

    return cases


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create a pool of candidate valid UTF-8 strings without NULs
    candidates = _make_cases(rng)

    # Also add a random-length printable ASCII string (up to 1024)
    rnd_len = rng.randint(1, 1024)
    candidates.append(_rand_printable_ascii(rng, rnd_len))

    # Pick one case and possibly trim to <=1024 UTF-8 bytes to align with stub limit
    s = rng.choice(candidates)

    # Ensure no NULs and valid UTF-8
    s = s.replace('\x00', '')
    data = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')

    if len(data) > 1024:
        # Trim without breaking UTF-8: back off to a codepoint boundary
        cut = 1024
        # Move back until at a valid boundary
        while cut > 0 and (data[cut-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
            cut -= 1
        data = data[:cut]

    # Return bytes; the fuzz harness will provide this to FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
    # We must not include a terminating NUL; the harness manages string lifetime.
    return bytes(data)
